title: NSGo game cutscene (version 2)
description:
Cutscene is one video or timeline cutscene, and the document a cutscene file holds.

Version 1 holds a video cutscene:

version: 1 source: asset:cutscenes/intro.mp4 group: cutscenes skippable: true skipAfter: 1.5s fit: cover

Version 2 holds either a video cutscene or an in-engine timeline cutscene with camera, actor, dialogue, sound and music tracks:

# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://game.nsgo.dev/schemas/cutscene.v2.json version: 2 kind: timeline scene: scenes/level_01.scene.yaml length: 12s skippable: true tracks: - kind: camera clips: - start: 0s duration: 1.6s easing: hold action: hold target: door

Parse reads such a file and Encode writes one, keys in the order of the fields below and zero values left out, so a file Encode wrote reads back and writes again unchanged.

version.description: Version is the file format's version, from MinVersion (1) to CurrentVersion (2), which Parse and Encode check. Player.Play and NewTimelinePlayer ignore it, so a cutscene made in code may leave it 0.

kind.description: Kind selects whether a version 2 cutscene plays a video ("video") or an in-engine timeline ("timeline"). Version 1 files leave it empty.

source.description: Source is the video for a video cutscene: an "asset:" path in the app's resources, a file path or a URL, as core.Video takes. Omitted on timeline cutscenes.

scene.description: Scene optionally names the scene file a timeline cutscene plays against, as a slash-separated path from the project root (for example "scenes/level_01.scene.yaml"). Used by game check and refs to validate object IDs. Version 2 timeline cutscenes only.

length.description: Length is the total duration of a timeline cutscene, written as a Go duration string such as "12s". Version 2 timeline cutscenes only.

group.description: Group is the mixer group whose volume, times the master volume, the cutscene's audio plays at; empty for the master volume alone (video) or per-track defaults (timeline).

skippable.description: Skippable lets the player skip the cutscene by a press, a skip key or back.

skipAfter.description: SkipAfter is how far into the cutscene a skippable cutscene must play before it can be skipped, so a press meant for the game before it does not skip it at once; 0 for from the start.

fit.description: Fit is how a video cutscene's picture fits the screen, FitContain when empty. Video cutscenes only.

transparent.description: Transparent leaves the screen behind a video cutscene clear rather than black, so the game shows in the bars and through a video with an alpha channel, where the platform keeps it (core.Video). Video cutscenes only.

tracks.description: Tracks are the ordered timeline tracks (camera, actor, dialogue, sound and music) of a timeline cutscene. Version 2 timeline cutscenes only.

Clip.description: Clip is one timed action or cue on a cutscene timeline track.

id.description: ID optionally identifies the clip for tools and editors; non-empty clip IDs must be unique within the cutscene.

label.description: Label is an optional human-readable label for the clip.

start.description: Start is when the clip begins on the timeline, as a Go duration string such as "1.6s".

duration.description: Duration is how long the clip lasts, as a Go duration string such as "2.4s".

easing.description: Easing is the interpolation curve for motion and camera pans: "linear" (default), "easeIn", "easeOut", "easeInOut" or "hold".

action.description: Action selects the operation on a camera track ("hold", "pan", "follow") or actor track ("walk", "state", "drop", "patrol").

target.description: Target is the scene object ID a camera clip holds on, pans to or follows.

fromX.description: FromX is the optional starting X coordinate for a camera pan or an actor walk, drop or patrol clip.

fromY.description: FromY is the optional starting Y coordinate for a camera pan or an actor walk, drop or patrol clip.

toX.description: ToX is the destination X coordinate for a camera hold/pan or an actor walk, drop or patrol clip.

toY.description: ToY is the destination Y coordinate for a camera hold/pan or an actor walk, drop or patrol clip.

offsetX.description: OffsetX is an optional horizontal camera offset applied when holding on, panning to or following a target object.

offsetY.description: OffsetY is an optional vertical camera offset applied when holding on, panning to or following a target object.

zoom.description: Zoom is the optional target camera zoom factor (positive) on a camera clip.

state.description: State is the animation state name played by an actor clip (required for "state" clips, optional for "walk", "drop" and "patrol").

speed.description: Speed is the optional travel speed in world units per second for an actor "patrol" clip; when omitted, patrol completes one full round-trip over Duration.

line.description: Line is the localization key (for example "intro.knight.01") shown by a dialogue clip; text lives in the l10n tables, not in the cutscene file.

speaker.description: Speaker optionally names who speaks a dialogue clip.

source.description: Source is the audio path or URI for a sound or music clip (for example "audio/door_slam.wav").

group.description: Group overrides the track's mixer group for a sound or music clip.

volume.description: Volume is the optional volume multiplier in [0, 1] for a sound or music clip; defaults to 1 when omitted.

fadeIn.description: FadeIn is the fade-in duration for a music clip, as a Go duration string such as "2s".

fadeOut.description: FadeOut is the fade-out duration for a music clip, as a Go duration string such as "1s".

loop.description: Loop repeats a music clip until its duration ends.

Track.description: Track is one lane on a timeline cutscene (camera, actor, dialogue, sound or music) holding timed clips.

id.description: ID optionally identifies the track for tools and editors; non-empty track IDs must be unique within the cutscene.

name.description: Name is an optional human-readable display label for the track.

kind.description: Kind selects what the track's clips drive: "camera", "actor", "dialogue", "sound" or "music".

target.description: Target is the scene object ID an actor track drives; required for "actor" tracks and omitted on other track kinds.

group.description: Group is the default mixer group for audio clips on a "sound" or "music" track (defaults to "sfx" for sound and "music" for music).

clips.description: Clips are the timed clips on this track, in non-decreasing start order.
